title: The other team uses Azure DevOps
scenario: "The client's second team lives in Azure DevOps. Same platform, same rules: no secrets, approvals, PR-based deploys." — Account lead (FEAT-08)
mission: Create a workload-identity-federation service connection, variable groups and an environment, and ship a small UI change through pipelines/azure-devops/app.yml.
objectives: Create a WIF service connection manually and trust it in Terraform
Compare GitHub and Azure DevOps side by side
Keep secrets out of pipeline variables

prerequisites.notes: Azure DevOps organization; companion lab-gitflow missions 0–7 recommended first.

steps.title: Service connection
steps.detail: Manual WIF connection; copy issuer and subject into ado_federated_* and apply 05-identity.

steps.title: Library and environment
steps.detail: Variable groups with non-secret values; environment with approval.

steps.title: Run app.yml
steps.detail: Small UI change; the pipeline builds, scans, pushes and opens the deploy PR on GitHub.

steps.title: Compare
steps.detail: Fill a side-by-side table: triggers, identity, approvals, artifact, deploy PR.

criteria.text: The Azure DevOps federated credential exists on its app
The latest app pipeline run succeeded
A deploy PR opened by the Azure DevOps pipeline exists on GitHub

expectedResult: Two CI/CD platforms, one platform contract.

concepts.title: Workload identity federation in Azure DevOps
concepts.body: A service connection of type "Workload identity federation" does the same as GitHub OIDC: Azure DevOps issues a token with a subject like `sc://<org>/<project>/<connection>`, and an Entra app trusts it. No secret is stored.

concepts.title: Library and environments
concepts.body: Variable groups (Pipelines → Library) hold shared non-secret values. Environments hold approvals and checks, evaluated when a deployment job targets them.

concepts.title: Same platform contract
concepts.body: The pipeline tool changes, the contract does not: CI builds and opens a deploy PR on GitHub; Argo CD deploys.

example.title: side-by-side vocabulary
example.body: GitHub reusable workflow ≈ ADO template; `environment:` ≈ deployment job environment; `azure/login` with OIDC ≈ `AzureCLI@2` with a WIF service connection.

glossary.def: ADO object that holds how a pipeline authenticates to an external service.

recovery: AADSTS700213: subject mismatch — compare the error subject with the federated credential.
dont: Do not create a secret-based service connection
Do not store secrets in plain pipeline variables
hints: addSpnToEnvironment exposes the federated token to scripts.
Templates + extends are the ADO equivalent of reusable workflows.

interview.question: Compare GitHub Actions and Azure DevOps for this platform: identity, approvals, reuse.
followUps: When would you recommend each to a client?

debrief: Both exchange a platform-issued OIDC token for an Entra token; the subject format differs. Approvals live on environments in both. The platform contract (CI writes Git, Argo CD deploys) stays identical.

checker.plan: Read-only: az ad app federated-credential list (ADO app), az pipelines runs list, gh pr list --author.
